question.text: DELTA of a call option is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: In standard option theory, the delta of a call option ranges between 0 and 1. A deep out-of-the-money call has a delta near 0 (insensitive to underlying moves), while a deep in-the-money call has a delta near 1 (moves nearly one-for-one with the underlying). Put deltas mirror this, ranging from -1 to 0. The Trap: "Always 1" and "always 0" describe only the extreme limits, not the typical range. "Infinity" is not a valid delta value — option price changes are bounded by the underlying's change. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook mentions delta as an option-based portfolio sensitivity measure but does not explicitly state the 0-to-1 range for a call delta. The framing above reflects general industry/regulatory knowledge of option Greeks.
